properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 15 at 4:59PM MDT until August 16 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...Aspen Acres Burn Scar

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, street
flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting
thunderstorms with heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may
lead to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel, and highways 165 and 78 in and around the
Aspen Acres Burn Scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 15 at 4:53PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 453 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Ellicott to 6 miles north of Hanover to 8
miles southeast of Fountain. Movement was east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Southeastern Colorado Springs, Fountain, Hanover, Truckton, Yoder,
Ellicott, Schriever Space Force Base, Security-Widefield, and Rush.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 15 at 4:31PM MDT until August 15 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 730 PM MDT.

* At 431 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and
0.5 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5
to 1 inch in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the North Saint Charles, South Creek,
Squirrel Creek, Middle Creek, and North Creek Drainages. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Highway 165, Beulah, Highway 78, stream crossings, and county roads
within and immediately downstream of the burn scar.

This includes the following high risk locations... Northcreek Road
county line to Red Mountain Camp and Northcreek Road from Red
Mountain Camp to Beulah.
properties.areaDesc: Custer, CO; Pueblo, CO

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 15 at 12:09PM MDT until August 15 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along Bijou Creek caused by excessive rainfall.

* WHERE...Rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek in northern
Elbert, Central Adams, Central Arapahoe, and southwestern Morgan
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along Bijou Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 1204 PM MDT, Local law enforcement reported flooding had
occurred along Bijou Creek through Adams County. Water had caused
closer of a couple county roads, but they have since reopened.
Water had also crested and spilled onto Colfax Avenue in rural
Adams County. The crest has passed this area, but will continue
moving downstream and affect areas farther north through the Hoyt
area and toward the confluence with the South Platte River in
Morgan County.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Bijou Creek and Bijou Creek.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 11:52AM MDT until August 15 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central and northeast Colorado, including the
following areas: the southern Front Range Foothills, Palmer Divide
area, I-25 corridor, and all of our eastern plains counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional thunderstorms and heavy rainfall this afternoon,
combined with the heavy rainfall from the past 3 days, will bring
a threat for flash flooding this afternoon and evening. Stronger
storms will be capable of producing 1 to 2 inches of rain in 30
minutes, with isolated areas receiving storm totals of 2 to 4
inches.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 11:32AM MDT until August 16 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central Colorado, including the following
area, Cheyenne CO and west central Kansas, including the following
areas, Gove, Greeley, Logan, Wallace and Wichita.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT  /7 PM CDT/ this evening through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1-3 inches of rain the past couple nights along with the
potential for another cluster or two of storms this evening and
overnight increases the potential for some flooding and even
flash flooding. Rainfall rates of 1.5 to 2.5 inches per hour is
possible in the strongest cells.
